facts.text: Ursine’s name, taken from the Latin word for bear, was chosen in 1895 to set it apart from other similarly named valleys.
A post office opened in Ursine in 1895 and stayed open until 1959, serving the remote community for over six decades.
Archaeologists find evidence of Native American occupation in the area dating back to about 5,500 B.C.E., while Mormon pioneers first settled the valley in 1863.
Ursine sits in Eagle Valley, nestled in the foothills of the White Rock Mountains and just two miles downstream from Eagle Valley Reservoir.
The climate is a semi‑arid high‑desert BSk, with hot, dry summers, cold snowy winters, and about 13 inches of annual precipitation.
By the early 20th century, Ursine hosted seven or eight ranching families, a one‑room schoolhouse, and community dances, though electricity didn’t arrive until the 1970s.
